name: python-package
body: A Python package or module as discovered by the Python frontend: a directory containing __init__.py or __init__.pyi is a package; nested packages compose a dotted identity by walking up init-bearing ancestors; a source file with no init-bearing ancestor is a flat top-level module whose identity is its file stem. The package/module is the unit of Python discovery and the parent of the files it contains — analogous to the Cargo manifest for Rust and the markdown document for Markdown. Its rendered Module FQN is `py.<module-identity>`: the language root (`py`) resolves the namespace-form open point and makes Python modules disjoint from every other language's root and from markdown's rooted absolute paths, so collision-freedom holds by construction across languages and for package-qualified dotted identities. It does NOT make flat init-less modules globally unique: a flat module's identity is its stem alone, so two same-stem init-less modules in different directories both render `py.<stem>` and the second is silently shadowed — flat modules are unique only within their directory (requirements.requirement.python-package-identity; requirements.note.python-frontend-open-points #1 DECIDED). Realised by the Python frontend.
